title: Signed line comparisons and their unbounded derived tensor action
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi on sites small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], associated to a finite-limit- and covering-preserving functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between sites with finite limits, with $R,S$ commutative and structural ring isomorphism $a:f^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. Let $P$ be an $R$-module sheaf on $\mathcal C$ and $Q$ an $S$-module sheaf on $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose both are locally free of rank one, meaning they restrict to the coefficient ring on a covering of the final object of their site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Put $F(M)=S\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and fix an isomorphism $t:F(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$.
Define $P^{[0]}=R$, $P^{[m]}=P^{\otimes_R m}$ for $m\ge1$, and $P^{[-m]}=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{[m]},R)$ for $m\ge1$, with $Q^{[d]}$ defined in the same way [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. There is a unique family of isomorphisms $t_d:F(P^{[d]})\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^{[d]}$ with the following normalization: $t_0$ is the coefficient-unit comparison and $t_1=t$; $t_{m+1}$ for $m\ge1$ is obtained from $t_m\otimes t$ by the canonical relative tensor comparison and the fixed right-associated powers; and, for $m\ge1$, $t_{-m}$ is characterized by
$$\operatorname{ev}_{Q^{[m]}}\circ(t_{-m}\otimes t_m)=(F\operatorname{ev}_{P^{[m]}})\circ\sigma^{-1},$$
with both sides mapped to $S$ by the unit comparison and $\sigma:F(P^{[-m]}\otimes_RP^{[m]})\cong F(P^{[-m]})\otimes_SF(P^{[m]})$. In particular it sends the pulled-back functional dual to a local basis of $P^{[m]}$ to the functional dual to its image under $t_m$. This family is natural in isomorphisms of the line data, and in scalar-extension identifications of these data: for commutative ring maps $R\to R'$, $S\to S'$ and a ring isomorphism $a':f^{-1}R'\xrightarrow{\sim}S'$ compatible with $a$, equip $P'=R'\otimes_RP$, $Q'=S'\otimes_SQ$ and $t'$ with the induced comparison; then its $t'_d$ is the scalar extension of $t_d$ under the canonical signed-power identifications.
The exact functor $F$ induces termwise pullback $D(F):D(R)\to D(S)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For every $K\in D(R)$ and $d\in\mathbf Z$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$D(F)(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P^{[d]}[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}D(F)(K)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Q^{[d]}[0],$$
namely the canonical derived tensor-pullback comparison followed by $1\otimes t_d[0]$. It respects the preceding unit, positive-power and evaluation normalizations. No boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor condition on $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Identify $S\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M$ with $f^{-1}M$ with its scalar action transported through $a$: the map is $s\otimes x\mapsto a^{-1}(s)x$, with inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The underlying abelian inverse image is exact by the site inverse-image theorem. The forgetful functors for module sheaves preserve kernels and cokernels and detect exactness, so $F$ is exact. Its coefficient-unit comparison $\epsilon:F(R)\to S$ is $s\otimes r\mapsto s\,a(r)$; its inverse sends $s$ to $s\otimes1$. These equations are equations of sheafified balanced tensors, so also apply on every slice.

For each $m\geq1$, $P^{[m]}$ and $Q^{[m]}$ are locally free of rank one. Indeed restriction to a localized site $\mathcal C/V$ commutes with sheaf tensor products, naturally and sending restricted pure tensors to pure tensors, by the localized-site tensor-restriction lemma; and by the definition of sheaf Hom together with relocalization, $\mathcal Hom_R(M,N)|_V=\mathcal Hom_{R|_V}(M|_V,N|_V)$. On a chart $P=Re$, iterated tensor gives $P^{[m]}=R e_m$, where $e_m=e^{\otimes m}$ with the stipulated brackets. By the definition of sheaf Hom its dual is $R e_m^\vee$, where $e_m^\vee(e_m)=1$. Evaluation is locally the map $r e_m^\vee\otimes s e_m\mapsto rs$ with inverse $r\mapsto r e_m^\vee\otimes e_m$. It is therefore globally an isomorphism by cover-local detection of isomorphisms. The same argument applies to $Q$ and also shows that all negative powers are lines. Changing $e_m$ to $v e_m$ changes $e_m^\vee$ to $v^{-1}e_m^\vee$, so the displayed evaluation and inverse are independent of the frame.

Write $\sigma_{A,B}:F(A\otimes_R B)\cong F(A)\otimes_S F(B)$ for the canonical tensor comparison. Put $t_0=\epsilon$ and $t_1=t$. Inductively set $t_{m+1}=(t_m\otimes t)\sigma_{P^{[m]},P}$, using the canonical rebracketings from $P^{[m+1]}$ to $P^{[m]}\otimes P$ and from $Q^{[m]}\otimes Q$ to $Q^{[m+1]}$ when necessary. Each factor is an isomorphism. This recursion proves existence and uniqueness for every nonnegative degree, by induction beginning at $m=1$. The associators invoked here are the actual sectionwise tensor associators of the closed symmetric monoidal module category; thus the phrase right-associated in the statement is interpreted with these explicit rebracketings, not as an equality of differently bracketed objects.

proof.text: For $m\geq1$ apply the finite-locally-free dual-pullback theorem to $L=P^{[m]}$, which is a line by step 2. It gives the evaluation-defined isomorphism $\delta_L:F(L^\vee)\cong(F L)^\vee$. Define $t_{-m}$ as $\delta_L$ followed by precomposition with $t_m^{-1}:Q^{[m]}\to F L$. The defining evaluation equation for $\delta_L$ is exactly $\operatorname{ev}_{Q^{[m]}}(t_{-m}\otimes t_m)=\epsilon\,F(\operatorname{ev}_L)\sigma^{-1}$. Conversely, precomposing an alleged such equation with $1\otimes t_m^{-1}$ specifies the pairing with every element of $Q^{[m]}$. The tensor-Hom adjunction then uniquely specifies $t_{-m}$. The dual-pullback theorem also gives the stated local dual-basis formula: the image functional takes $t_m(F e_m)$ to $1$. This proves existence, uniqueness and the basis assertion for all negative degrees.

For isomorphisms $b:P\to\widetilde P$ and $c:Q\to\widetilde Q$ satisfying $\widetilde t\,F(b)=c\,t$, extend $b,c$ to positive powers by tensoring and to negative powers by precomposition with the inverses of their positive powers. In degree zero use the identity of the coefficient ring. Naturality of $\sigma$ and the recursion give $\widetilde t_m F(b_m)=c_m t_m$ for $m\geq0$. For negative $m$ this equality follows by applying the contravariant naturality of $\delta$ to $b_m$, then precomposing with the inverses in the preceding equality. Equivalently, both sides satisfy the same evaluation equation, whose uniqueness was proved in step 4. This proves naturality in isomorphisms of line data.

proof.text: Let $E_R=R'\otimes_R-$ and $E_S=S'\otimes_S-$, and let $F'$ use $a'$. The canonical comparison $\beta_M:F'E_RM\cong E_SFM$ is obtained by applying the normalized inverse-image tensor comparison to $R'\otimes_R M$ and balancing: both expressions identify with $S'\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M$. In one direction the scalar formula is $s'\otimes(r'\otimes x)\mapsto s'a'(f^{-1}r')\otimes x$; in the other it is $s'\otimes x\mapsto s'\otimes(1\otimes x)$. The balancing relation and compatibility of $a,a'$ show these are inverse. The normalized pure-tensor formulas for inverse image and scalar extension show that this comparison preserves insertion of $1$ and binary tensor products. For example both routes send $1\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(1\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$; coefficient multiples follow by linearity and these pure tensors generate the sheafified tensor locally. Thus $t'=E_S(t)\beta_P$ and induction using the tensor-power scalar comparisons identifies $t'_m$ with $E_S(t_m)$ for every $m\geq0$.

For negative degrees use the scalar-extension dual isomorphisms on $P^{[m]}$ and $Q^{[m]}$. They preserve evaluation: on a free chart, scalar extension carries $e_m^\vee$ to the functional dual to $1\otimes e_m$ (also the finite-free dual theorem applied to the identity site functor with coefficient map $R\to R'$). Likewise it carries the functional dual to $t_m(F e_m)$ to the functional dual to $1\otimes t_m(F e_m)$. Hence after the signed-power identifications, extension of the evaluation equation for $t_{-m}$ becomes precisely the primed equation with $t'_m$, by step 6. Uniqueness from step 4 identifies it with $t'_{-m}$. The computation is on covering slice charts; equality globally follows from uniqueness of amalgamations for sheaves. There is no flatness assumption on $R\to R'$ or $S\to S'$: the dual-pullback theorem explicitly allows arbitrary structural ring maps.

source.place: Tags 0GMX and 0FNY; scalar-extension blueprint paragraph (3), expanded using evaluation.

proof.text: Because $F$ is exact by step 1, termwise application carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and gives $D(F):D(R)\to D(S)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The exact-functor derived theorem identifies this functor, with its termwise comparison, with the total left derived module pullback $Lf^*$. Thus $D(F)(M[0])=F(M)[0]$ under the canonical comparison, and no resolution or boundedness is needed to compute $D(F)$ on a complex.

The evaluation isomorphisms of step 2 and the tensor associators identify tensoring with a line with an equivalence, with inverse tensoring with its dual. An equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties, so tensoring with each $P^{[d]}$ or $Q^{[d]}$ is exact; hence these sheaves are flat. A single flat sheaf in degree zero is K-flat by the bounded-above-flat theorem. Consequently the ordinary tensor products and evaluations among these degree-zero lines represent their derived tensor products and evaluations. This uses only a boundedness statement about the one-term line complexes, not about $K$.

Apply the unbounded derived tensor-pullback theorem with inputs $K$ and $P^{[d]}[0]$, and replace $Lf^*$ by $D(F)$ using step 8. It gives $D(F)(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P^{[d]}[0])\cong D(F)K\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}F(P^{[d]})[0]$. Follow it by $1\otimes t_d[0]$ to obtain the asserted isomorphism. Bifunctoriality of that theorem makes this natural in every derived morphism of $K$, and step 5 gives naturality in line isomorphisms. The theorem is explicitly on ordinary unbounded categories for arbitrary ringed topoi, so neither finite Tor amplitude, constructibility nor boundedness of $K$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), applied to the line in degree zero.

proof.text: The derived tensor comparison is the canonical strong monoidal one: its associator and unit diagrams commute by the ringed derived monoidal-comparison theorem. On the line complexes, step 9 identifies the derived tensor products and evaluations with the ordinary ones. The canonical comparison of the derived tensor-pullback theorem is the one computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms, where $Lf^*$ is termwise $F$ (step 8) and derived tensor is the total tensor complex; hence on the one-term flat lines its component at $(P^{[m]}[0],P[0])$ is $\sigma_{P^{[m]},P}[0]$, and at the evaluation pairing it is $\sigma[0]$ as used in steps 3 and 4. Substitute the equation $t_{m+1}=(t_m\otimes t)\sigma$ into the associator diagram; it gives precisely the positive-power normalization of the comparison in step 10, including the fixed rebracketings. The unit diagram gives the case $d=0$. Substitute $\operatorname{ev}_Q(t_{-m}\otimes t_m)=\epsilon F(\operatorname{ev}_P)\sigma^{-1}$ into the naturality diagram for evaluation; it gives the evaluation normalization. Tensoring each such commuting diagram with $D(F)K$ preserves its equality. The representative comparisons in the monoidal theorem are the canonical K-flat ones, so this verifies the specified maps on the unbounded categories, rather than just existence of abstract isomorphisms.
